steps.tx: A **Chauffeur fracture**, historically designated as a Hutchinson fracture, is an intra-articular shear fracture of the radial styloid process. The eponym originated from early twentieth-century automobile chauffeurs whose wrists were struck violently by backfiring hand-crank starter levers. The fracture line begins in the scaphoid fossa of the distal radius and courses obliquely into the radiocarpal joint.
steps.say: A Chauffeur or Hutchinson fracture is an intra-articular break of the radial styloid. The name comes from old cars where a backfiring starting crank kicked back against the chauffeur wrist. The fracture begins in the scaphoid facet and runs obliquely into the wrist joint.

steps.tx: The contemporary **injury mechanism** combines forced wrist dorsiflexion with ulnar deviation. During impact, the hard convex proximal pole of the scaphoid drives forcefully against the radial styloid, shearing it off. Alternatively, extreme tension along the robust radioscaphocapitate and radiolunate ligaments avulses the styloid tip during severe supination-adduction trauma.
steps.say: Today, it happens when falling on a dorsiflexed, ulnar-deviated hand. The dense scaphoid punches like a wedge against the radial styloid, shearing it off. Strong extrinsic ligaments can also avulse the styloid tip under severe tension.

left.title: Direct Impaction Mechanism
points: Wrist in dorsiflexion and ulnar deviation

steps.tx: The essential diagnostic pitfall is missing **scapholunate dissociation**, which frequently accompanies radial styloid fractures. When the styloid shears, tensile failure often tears the interosseous scapholunate ligament. A posteroanterior radiograph reveals the pathognomonic Terry Thomas sign, defined as a widened scapholunate joint space exceeding three millimeters, often accompanied by scaphoid ring sign on flexion views.
steps.say: Always check for scapholunate ligament tears. When the styloid breaks, the force frequently tears the scapholunate ligament too. Look for the Terry Thomas sign, where the gap between the scaphoid and lunate widens beyond three millimeters, resembling the gap between the famous actor front teeth.

steps.tx: Anatomic **articular reduction** is mandatory because even one millimeter of persistent joint incongruity within the scaphoid fossa accelerates post-traumatic radiocarpal osteoarthritis. In minimally displaced fractures, closed reduction under traction followed by percutaneous fixation using two cannulated cancellous lag screws or Kirschner wires under fluoroscopic guidance achieves excellent stability.
steps.say: You must achieve perfect joint surface alignment. Even one millimeter of articular step-off in the scaphoid facet causes rapid cartilage wear and painful wrist arthritis. If closed reduction aligns the joint, insert two percutaneous cannulated lag screws to compress the fragment rigidly.

steps.tx: Surgical **plate fixation** with a pre-contoured radial buttress plate is indicated whenever comminution, rotation, or displacement exceeds one millimeter. The buttress plate counteracts the proximal shearing vector exerted by the brachioradialis tendon, which inserts directly onto the radial styloid. Postoperative splinting for four weeks allows rigid osseous consolidation before progressive wrist rehabilitation.
steps.say: When comminution or displacement exceeds one millimeter, use a radial buttress plate. The brachioradialis muscle inserts directly onto the radial styloid, constantly trying to pull it proximally. A stout buttress plate neutralizes this deforming tendon pull and secures the joint line.

vis.title: Management Algorithm
rows: Splint for 4 weeks then active range of motion
ORIF with buttress plate plus ligament repair

quiz.q: Which muscle tendon inserts directly onto the fractured fragment in a Chauffeur fracture?
quiz.explain: The brachioradialis inserts into the base of the radial styloid process, creating a proximal deforming vector across a Chauffeur fracture.

quiz.q: What width of scapholunate gap on a posteroanterior wrist radiograph confirms a positive Terry Thomas sign?
quiz.explain: A scapholunate distance greater than 3 mm on a PA wrist radiograph indicates tear of the scapholunate interosseous ligament (the Terry Thomas sign).
